text:
A: Hiya! Oh, hello, can you hear me alright?
B: Yes. Hello.
A: I'm Joanne, I'm in Taunton, down in Somerset. That's three of these I've done now, I'm getting the hang of it!
B: Shahida. Ilford. Last one for me also.
A: Oh, lovely. Have the others been nice? I've had a mechanic and an archivist, would you believe. Sorry, I'm already waffling!
B: The mechanic, yes, I had him also. He doesn't eat properly, that boy.
A: Ha! Oh, I did wonder. Energy drinks and pasties, I bet. My son's the same, he's twenty-two, lives in Bristol, comes home weekends with a bag of washing.
B: That photo in your kitchen, on the window, those are your children? I thought grandchildren.
A: Oh, bless you, no, that's Callum and Ellie! Although some days I feel old enough to be a nan. Have you got grandchildren?
B: Five. Two I look after, my elder son's. Two days a week I pick up from school, I give them dinner, homework, then he comes. Seven and five. The little one, very clever, very naughty.
A: Oh, they're the best ones, the naughty clever ones. What do you cook them?
B: Proper food. Daal, roti, chicken. I make the roti fresh every day. Forty years I'm making same food, nobody complains.
A: Well, if it's not broke! I'm a shepherd's pie and roast sort of cook, and curries from a jar, but I jazz them up, you know, bit of extra garlic. You'd probably be horrified.
B: Jar curry, hm. It's ok. Everybody is busy.
A: That's very diplomatic of you! What did you used to do? Before, I mean, if you did work?
B: Ladies' clothing shop, Green Street. Suits, fabric. Fifteen years. I stopped at sixty, my knees.
A: Oh, knees and backs, honestly, the whole lot of us are falling apart. I was a vet nurse twenty years and my back finished me off. I do a bit at a cat rescue now, unpaid, but I'd love to find something part-time, sitting down. I just worry I'm out of the loop now, you know, three years off, everything's on computers. Sorry, does that make sense?
B: You can learn computer. I did computer course at the library, ten years ago, I was nearly sixty. Now I do surveys, WhatsApp, everything.
A: Oh, that's really encouraging, actually.
B: Twenty years nurse, you know animals, you know people. Somebody will take you. Don't say "only" this, "only" that.
A: Oh, gosh. Thank you. That's, erm, that's just what I needed to hear really.
B: Hm. That's it.
A: Do you sew? Sorry, I'm guessing, it's the fabric shop.
B: Yes, all the family, I do alterations. Weddings, I take in, take out. They don't pay me, of course.
A: Same as my traybakes for church! Nobody ever pays for a traybake.
B: You have nice house, your kitchen. Very clean.
A: Oh, it's not always, I'd tidied for the camera!
B: Acha. I think time is finishing now.
